description.narrative:
To contribute towards an accountable and responsive government working with active citizens to satisfactorily implement pro-poor policies.
The ZGF provided comprehensive grants and capacity development support to Zambian civil society organisations (CSOs) in all 10 of the country's provinces. The organisation was supported through a basket funding arrangement known as the Joint Financing Agreement (JFA) with contributions from the Department for International Development (DFID), Danish International Development Agency (DANIDA), Irish Aid, Swedish International Development Agency (Sida) and Deutsche Gesellschaft fr Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ).

ZGF is a re-granting institution providing financial support and capacity building for civil society organisations in Zambia. ZGF's partners are both well-established and, increasingly so, smaller organisations and groupings who can grow stronger and more professional with the support of ZGF. With its support of 80 MSEK over three years Sweden is the biggest cooperating partner.

ZGF vidareförmedlar medel till organisationer i det civila samhället och tillhandahåller kapacitetsutveckling kring organisatorisk oc finansiell styrning samt i de ämnen som organisationerna själva efterfrågar stöd i. Bland ZGF:s partner finns etablerade organisationer och mindre organisationer och grupper som med ZGF:s stöd kan växa sig starkare och mer professionella.

ZGF and its Grant Partners have scored numerous achievements over the JFA II period. Most notable of these are the increased number of CSOs that became actively engaged with duty bearers at different levels by initiating a wide range of policy engagement activities to address specific issues of concern, and the significant increase in the number of communities that are making demands on duty bearers and having their issues resolved. In addition, improvements were noted in CSOs financial management capacities, and improvements in the overall organisational capacity that has been built in CSOs as a result of learning opportunities and other capacity development interventions that ZGF made available.
In total, ZGF successfully managed 96 grants during the period under review. The demand for these grants was considerable, with 390 applications received. However, a significant proportion of these were rejected (294 = 75%). Most GPs have been successful in completing their projects.
ZGF was rated very effective in capacity development (CD) and it developed a wide range of CD tools and introduced a variety of methods in this regard, e.g. training, mentoring, learning and sharing events. The training models in particular proved to be specifically efficient. Altogether, 1,758 participants were reached during the period under review and the trainings included topics such as strategic management and planning, financial management and gender mainstreaming. Different tool kits were produced for use by GPs. Improvements were also noted in CSOs financial management capacities as well as in the overall organisational capacity. This resulted from learning opportunities and other capacity development interventions that ZGF made available.
An increase in the number of GPs with functional M&E (monitoring and evaluation) systems at organisational level was reported in 2015. The partners were reported using the various tools and processes that they have developed for collection and analysis of data, reporting and other M&E requirements. This means that it is not solely the pure availability of these tools that have been of importance, but other specific attributes, such as the extent to which GPs utilise their tools and processes to report and provide evidence on the outcomes of their projects. An analysis of the progress reports received throughout 2015 showed that all 44 GPs were able to report some form of outcome level results. This suggests an appreciation of the GPs need and desire to show results, as opposed to only mentioning them. This resulted in a new layer of legitimacy to their policy influencing work.
Another result achieved was the increasing number of GPs demonstrating community involvement and ensuring that gender is mainstreamed. Of the 44 GPs with active contracts in 2015, 29 actively involved communities in different ways in their work. For example, comprehensive training for community members in six districts on social accountability and advocacy (CSPR) was conducted as well as quarterly dialogue meetings between communities, the Mayor and members of Parliament to discuss environmental issues in Livingstone (EAT). In total, GPs reported that they had involved 183 communities across all 10 provinces, reaching a total of 54,458 people (at least 49% female). This means that approximately 70% of GPs could involve communities in their work, creating real opportunities for citizen involvement at different levels. Adding to this, 107 (approximately 60%) of these communities went on to engage duty bearers at different levels, claiming their rights and engaging in policy. For example, the Kateshi community in Kasama convinced the chief to reprimand parents who perpetrated child labour instead of having them attend school.
ZGF was an efficient intermediary organisation that provided value for money services for both Cooperating Partners (CPs) and GPs. The bulk of funds went to grants and capacity development, in line with the objectives set out. The capacity development provided to CSOs to both manage funds and achieve results contributed to the Swedish strategy.
The approach set out by the ZGF, for instance, to focus on Capacity Development and not only grant making, led to sustainable CSOs even if no future JFA materialised.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
